title: OKC Thunder: Seattle's Ghost, Presti's Picks
description: A bitter relocation, a UCLA guard taken fourth, a mountain of future assets, and a new MVP face—five steps into Thunder basketball.
imageHint: The electric blue and orange of Paycom Center with passionate fans creating one of the NBA's loudest atmospheres

questions.question: After Clay Bennett won a bitter arena fight in Seattle, the SuperSonics relocated south and became the Thunder. In what year did the move happen?
questions.explanation: Seattle kept the SuperSonics name and colors in limbo; Oklahoma City got a franchise and a roar. Sam Presti, already GM, kept drafting through the chaos.

questions.question: That same 2008 draft night—still under the Sonics name—Presti took which UCLA guard fourth overall, later nicknamed "The Brodie"?
questions.explanation: Durant was already there from the last Sonics draft in 2007. Presti also grabbed Serge Ibaka at 24 that night. Westbrook became the heartbeat—and the triple-double machine.

questions.question: Westbrook later averaged a triple-double for a full season—the first to do so since which legend's lonely 1961–62 mark?
questions.explanation: Robertson's season stood alone for 54 years until Westbrook matched it in 2016–17—then did it again. "Why not?" became a slogan and a dare.

questions.question: After Westbrook matched Oscar Robertson then left OKC, which scoring guard—snagged in the 2019 Paul George trade—became the new face of the Thunder?
questions.explanation: Quiet footwork, endless midrange, MVP chatter. While SGA climbed, Presti was busy doing what Presti does: collecting future firsts like trading cards.

questions.question: Around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Presti turned departing stars into a mountain of what future NBA asset—then flipped those into even more?
questions.explanation: Stars out, firsts in, firsts into more firsts. By the mid-2020s the Thunder held an absurd pile of upcoming selections—the long game Seattle never got to finish.

easterEgg.title: Last Sonics draft
easterEgg.text: Kevin Durant was the last SuperSonics draft pick—No. 2 in 2007—before the move. He won MVP in Oklahoma City, reached the 2012 Finals, then left. The franchise's ghost and its future have been arguing ever since.
